title: Edgar Codd and the Relational Model (1970)
explainer: The normal forms you apply in this project trace directly to Edgar F. Codd's 1970 paper, 'A Relational Model of Data for Large Shared Data Banks,' written while he was a researcher at IBM. Codd proposed representing data as simple tables of rows and columns governed by first-order logic, replacing the hierarchical and network database designs common at the time, and introduced normalization as a way to eliminate redundancy and the update anomalies it causes. IBM was initially slow to adopt the idea, partly because it had revenue tied to its existing hierarchical IMS/DB system; Codd won the 1981 ACM Turing Award for the work.
